entities.summary:
Adam Dyczkowski (1932–2018) was a Polish Catholic bishop who served as Bishop of Zielona Góra-Gorzów and later as Bishop of Kalisz, navigating the Church's challenging position within communist and then post-communist Poland. Ordained a priest of the Poznań archdiocese, he was appointed bishop in 1986, during the final turbulent years of the Polish People's Republic.

Dyczkowski served across the period of Poland's Solidarity movement, the imposition of martial law, and the eventual transition to democracy in 1989. As a bishop in western Poland—a region whose postwar German-to-Polish population transfer made religious identity politically sensitive—he worked to integrate a community still processing its own displacement and resettlement. His pastoral work engaged questions of German-Polish reconciliation and the healing of historical wounds in the borderland dioceses.

After 1989, Dyczkowski participated in the postcommunist reorganisation of Polish Church structures, including the creation of new dioceses as Poland's ecclesiastical map was rationalised. He served as Bishop of Kalisz after its creation as an independent diocese. His career spanned the full arc of Polish Catholic experience from communist persecution to institutional expansion, representing the Church's enduring presence through systemic political transformation.
